scope: The PeakPickerHiRes TOPP wrapper (package P3-PICKER-TOOL of the early TOPP bundle, extended by P4-PICKER-LOWMEM): registration, the in-memory run, the -processOption lowmemory run, and the parameter-failure and -write_ini behaviour. Sources and fixtures come from the independently versioned OpenMS4-cli, OpenMS4-topp and OpenMS4-test-data packages and are deliberately not resolved against the Core SDK checkout; the core PeakPickerHiRes sources are listed as context, because the picker itself is tests/data/peak_picking_provenance.json.
method: The wrapper is transcribed from the pinned C++ tool. The four in-memory registrations, the six parameter failures and TOPPWRITEINI_OVERWRITE are reproduced through cli::run_with in a per-case temporary directory. XML outputs are compared by decoded content (decision D6): counts, ids, levels, types and array names exactly, every m/z, retention time, intensity and float array value bit for bit, and the full decoded walk with exact numbers over container-neutral processing records. INI outputs are compared line by line with the ported FuzzyDiff and the registered whitelists. The two low-memory registrations TOPP_PeakPickerHiRes_3 and _4 are reproduced the same way. Their retained expectations, and the three C++ outputs listed under cpp_release_outputs, were regenerated by the optimised C++ Release install at these pins on ibminode06 (oracle ../oracle/p4-lowmemory): the Release build reproduced both retained upstream files byte for byte, so comparing against them is comparing against that build's own output. FuzzyDiff cannot be used across the two implementations here - it stops on line 1 column 31 at the ISO-8859-1 against UTF-8 declaration - so the cross-implementation comparison is the decoded one (decision D6).
evidence_tier: executed differential (tier 1): retained upstream outputs, and C++ outputs produced by the prebuilt product SDK (Debug, core 4fdec46, decision D7) recorded in the two oracle manifests below

determinism: The picker is serial, as the source is. In-memory: -threads 1, 2, 16 and 0 produce byte-identical output. Low-memory: the mode is serial by construction in both implementations - the source's consumer dispatch loop hands over one record at a time and this port's reader does the same - and -threads 1, 8 and 32 were confirmed byte-identical for both the C++ Release build and the Rust release binary on ibminode06 (oracle ../oracle/p4-lowmemory, case `threads`), as well as in the test suite on two inputs.
target_verification: cargo test --locked --no-default-features --features mzml,paramxml --test topp_peak_picker_hi_res --lib on stable and 1.85.0 (ibmi dax); clippy --locked --all-features --all-targets -D warnings; doc --locked --all-features --no-deps; release builds of the PeakPickerHiRes binary with default features and with mzml,paramxml on both toolchains. Instrument scale (ibminode06, release, outside the gates): the 2.3 GB UK222.mzML benchmark input loads through the tool's options and, with the sibling lane that lifts the picker's pooled acquisition-copy ledger, is picked end to end; 22,776,198 centroids bit-identical to the C++ Release output. ../oracle/topp-peak-picker-scale/manifest.json has the numbers.

shows: trunc, garbage, badb64: C++ exit 3 in BOTH process options with an 'Unable to read file' message, a zero-byte low-memory output and no in-memory output. badcount: C++ low memory exit 0 writing <spectrumList count="9"> over five records, C++ in memory exit 0 with count="5". This is the executed evidence for 'the one place this port is stricter' - the port writes the same lying count over a closed document and then reports it. Pinned by a_low_memory_run_reports_a_lying_list_count_over_a_closed_document.
badlen, badrt, dupid: C++ exit 0 in both modes where this port exits 3 in both modes. A reader strictness difference identical in the two process options, not part of the low-memory specification.

am1 (-algorithm:ms_levels 2 with SignalToNoise:auto_mode 1): C++ writes all five records and dies of SIGSEGV (exit 139) leaving 404,915 bytes with no index, because a signal runs no destructor; this port exits 11 over a closed, indexed document holding its one written record. The source is therefore not comparable on the path a_failure_after_the_first_record_still_closes_the_document pins, which asserts the ~MSDataWritingConsumer/doCleanup_ contract instead.

the healthy low-memory run is unchanged by the fix: C++ sha256 91b0fdb0... equals the retained PeakPickerHiRes_output_lowMem.mzML and the Rust release binary writes 0037871e..., the bytes recorded before the fix.

The C++ second pass decodes and hands over in batches of 100 records (PeakFileOptions.h:248, MzMLHandler.cpp:198-244 and 259-274), so a corrupt record kills its whole batch before any of it reaches the writer: on the five-record input the C++ low-memory run writes 0 bytes whichever record is corrupt (first, third, last).

On a 110-spectrum FileMerger output with spectrum 104 corrupted, the C++ low-memory run exits 3 leaving 875,255 bytes - the 100 records of the first batch, a closed </mzML>, an index and a fileChecksum, under the announced count="110". This is the executed evidence that the source's destructor leaves a closed partial document, which is what a_failure_after_the_first_record_still_closes_the_document asserts for this port.

Found in the fix round and RESOLVED in the close round: on the HEALTHY 110-spectrum FileMerger output the C++ low-memory run writes all 110 records, and this port then stopped after five with 'record needs a different mzML sourceFileList or dataProcessingList than the header written for the first record' (exit 11), because each merged part carries its own dataProcessing. Recorded as native difference 12. The lead ruled that the source's behaviour there is defined and must be reproduced, so MSDataWritingConsumer gained ReferencePolicy and the tool's low-memory path selects SourceDangling; the close-round differential shows this port now writing the same 110 records with the same dangling identifiers. The figure quoted here at the time, '109 dangling references', was the reference COUNT: the measured dangling count is 105, dp_sp_5 through dp_sp_109, records 1 to 4 needing none. See close_round_differential.
